input.name: Greeting flow
input.goal: Greet a person after their name is available.

stages.name: get-name
stages.prompt: Obtain the user's name and return it as plain text. Pause only if an answer from the user is required.

stages.name: say-hello
stages.prompt: Write a greeting using the name in the input.

input.name: spanish-lessons
input.goal:
Keep the Spanish lesson summaries up to date. Find the lessons in the shared
transcription document that have not been summarized yet and store one
summary document per lesson in DocuMur project "Spanish Lessons" (ID <project-id>).

Use the DocuMur MCP tools (list_documents, get_document, create_document,
edit_document, media__download_file_by_url, media__get_file).

There is no human in the loop. If you need user input, pause the flow with a question.

stages.name: find-last-processed-lesson
stages.prompt:
Find the last processed lesson in DocuMur project <project-id>.

Lesson summary documents are named by the lesson date, formatted
YYYY-MM-DD. List the documents in the project with list_documents and
pick the one with the latest date in its name.

Return:
  - document_id: the ID of that document.
  - lesson_date: its date, formatted YYYY-MM-DD.

stages.name: find-new-lessons
stages.prompt:
Download the file <transcription-document-url>
with media__download_file_by_url and read it with media__get_file.

The file contains Spanish lesson materials. Find the lessons that are
newer than the last processed lesson from the input. Start reading from
the end of the file so you don't process the whole history.

Return:
  - media_file_id: the media file ID used to read the transcription.
  - new_lessons: the new lessons, oldest first, each with:
    - lesson_date: the lesson date, formatted YYYY-MM-DD.
    - start_row: the row where the lesson starts in the transcription.
    - end_row: the row where the lesson ends in the transcription.

If there are no new lessons, return an empty new_lessons list.

stages.name: create-lesson-summaries
stages.prompt:
Prepare a summary of every lesson in the input's new_lessons and store
each one as a document in project <project-id>.

If new_lessons is empty, finish the stage with an empty list.

Process the lessons one at a time, oldest first. After storing a lesson,
save the list of processed lesson dates as the stage output. When the
stage resumes, skip the lessons already listed in the saved output.

For each lesson:

SOURCE
The lesson transcription is in the media file `media_file_id`, between
the lesson's start_row and end_row. Read only that range.

TARGET DOCUMENT
- The document name is the lesson date, formatted exactly YYYY-MM-DD.
- If a document with that name already exists in the project, EDIT it.
  Never create a second document for the same date.
- Before writing, read one existing lesson summary in the project so
  your output matches the established house style.

STRUCTURE
Use exactly these markdown sections, in this order. Omit a whole section
only when the lesson genuinely contains nothing for it.

# Lesson <YYYY-MM-DD>

## New Grammar
One bullet per grammar point taught in this lesson. State the rule, then
give the lesson's own example in Spanish.

## New Vocabulary
One bullet per new non-verb word or phrase, formatted `word — English
meaning`. Include the article for nouns (el / la). No verbs here.

## New Verbs
One `###` subsection per new verb, titled with the infinitive, each
followed by a conjugation table.

VERB TABLE RULES — follow these exactly; this is the part most often
done wrong:
- Columns, in this order:
  | pronoun | presente | pretérito indefinido | imperfecto | futuro | presente de subjuntivo |
- Rows, in this order: yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros, vosotros,
  ellos/ellas/ustedes
- FILL EVERY CELL. Supply the complete conjugation from your own
  knowledge of Spanish grammar. Do NOT leave a cell blank merely because
  that form did not appear in the lesson. A table with empty cells is a
  failed lesson.
- Mark irregular forms with a trailing asterisk, e.g. `hago*`.
- The infinitive belongs in the `###` heading, not in a table column.

The conjugation tables are reference material produced from standard
Spanish grammar — they are deliberately NOT extracted from the
transcription. Only the grammar points and the vocabulary must come from
this lesson.

WHAT COUNTS AS NEW
A word, phrase or verb is new when this lesson introduces, corrects or
explains it. Do not pad the summary with words merely used in passing.

Return the list of processed lesson dates, formatted YYYY-MM-DD.

Keep documents sorted by date.

Run lesson processing in parallel using sub-agents.
